mcqs.q: Malignant melanoma is a malignant tumour of:
mcqs.explain: Melanoma is an aggressive malignant neoplasm of melanocytes.

mcqs.q: In the radial growth phase, melanoma cells:
opts: Spread horizontally within the superficial epithelium
mcqs.explain: The radial (superficial spreading) phase expands horizontally within the superficial epithelium — a better-prognosis phase.

mcqs.q: The vertical growth phase is characterised by:
opts: Deep infiltration with a palpable nodule
mcqs.explain: The vertical growth phase (VGP) shows deep infiltration and a palpable nodule — aggressive behaviour.

mcqs.q: Which melanoma shows ONLY a vertical growth phase?
mcqs.explain: Nodular melanoma has only a vertical growth phase, making it the most aggressive type.

mcqs.q: Which is the MOST aggressive cutaneous melanoma subtype?
mcqs.explain: Nodular melanoma is the most aggressive because of its pure vertical growth phase.

mcqs.q: Lentigo maligna melanoma typically arises on:
mcqs.explain: Lentigo maligna melanoma occurs on sun-exposed skin (face) and has the best prognosis.

mcqs.q: Which subtype carries the BEST prognosis?
mcqs.explain: Lentigo maligna melanoma is slow-growing and has the best prognosis.

mcqs.q: Acral-lentiginous melanoma characteristically involves the:
mcqs.explain: Acral-lentiginous melanoma arises on palms/soles and may pigment the nail bed; it is very aggressive with a poorer prognosis.

mcqs.q: The most common cutaneous melanoma subtype overall is:
mcqs.explain: Superficial spreading melanoma is the most common type and has a prolonged radial growth phase.

mcqs.q: In the ABCDE rule, 'A' stands for:
mcqs.explain: A = Asymmetry; B = Border irregularity; C = Colour variation; D = Diameter >6 mm; E = Elevation/Evolution.

mcqs.q: In the ABCDE rule, 'D' refers to a diameter greater than:
mcqs.explain: D = Diameter greater than 6 mm is a warning sign.

mcqs.q: In the ABCDE rule, 'B' stands for:
mcqs.explain: B = Border irregularity (notched/uneven edges).

mcqs.q: In the ABCDE rule, 'E' stands for:
mcqs.explain: E = Elevation or Evolution (a changing lesion).

mcqs.q: Oral malignant melanoma represents approximately what proportion of oral malignancies?
mcqs.explain: Oral melanoma is rare — about 0.5% of all oral malignancies.

mcqs.q: Oral malignant melanoma shows which sex and age pattern?
mcqs.explain: Oral melanoma favours males, older age (4th–7th decade), and blacks/Asians over whites.

mcqs.q: The classic intraoral site of malignant melanoma is the:
mcqs.explain: Most oral melanomas occur on the hard palate and maxillary alveolar ridge.

mcqs.q: Early oral melanoma typically appears as a lesion that is:
mcqs.explain: Early lesions are flat (macular) and become nodular as they progress to the vertical growth phase.

mcqs.q: Which immunohistochemical marker is essentially 100% positive in melanoma?
mcqs.explain: Melan-A ~100%, HMB-45 ~95.5%, S-100 ~90% positivity in melanoma.

mcqs.q: S-100 positivity in melanoma is approximately:
mcqs.explain: S-100 is positive in about 90% of melanomas (sensitive but less specific than HMB-45/Melan-A).

mcqs.q: HMB-45 positivity in melanoma is approximately:
mcqs.explain: HMB-45 is positive in about 95.5% of melanomas.

mcqs.q: Clark levels describe the:
opts: Depth (level) of invasion through tissue layers
mcqs.explain: Clark levels grade the anatomic depth of invasion; Breslow measures thickness — both prognostic.

mcqs.q: A pigmented palatal lesion that is enlarging, nodular and bleeding should be managed by:
mcqs.explain: A changing/nodular pigmented palatal lesion must be biopsied to exclude melanoma.

mcqs.q: Compared with an amalgam tattoo, a melanoma is more likely to:
mcqs.explain: Melanoma evolves (enlarges, changes colour, becomes nodular); amalgam tattoo is static and may be radio-opaque.

mcqs.q: Mucosal lentiginous melanoma differs from cutaneous types mainly by its:
mcqs.explain: Mucosal lentiginous melanoma arises on mucosa (e.g. oral); it is included in the melanoma classification.

mcqs.q: The poorest-prognosis melanoma among these acral/nodular forms is associated with:
mcqs.explain: Early vertical growth and deep invasion (nodular/acral) worsen prognosis; a long radial phase is more favourable.

mcqs.q: Why are blacks and Asians over-represented in ORAL melanoma?
opts: Oral melanoma is relatively more common in these groups
mcqs.explain: Although cutaneous melanoma is commoner in fair skin, ORAL melanoma is relatively more frequent in blacks and Asians.

mcqs.q: Identify the lesion of the palate/maxillary alveolus shown.
mcqs.explain: Irregular, expanding black pigmentation of the palate/maxillary alveolus is the classic site of oral melanoma.

mcqs.q: Identify this raised, darkly pigmented skin lesion.
mcqs.explain: A raised, darkly pigmented nodule with vertical growth is nodular melanoma — the most aggressive type.

mcqs.q: This melanoma of the sole, which may also pigment the nail, is:
mcqs.explain: Melanoma of palms/soles with nail-bed pigmentation is acral-lentiginous — aggressive, poorer prognosis.

mcqs.q: This irregular brown patch on sun-damaged facial skin is:
mcqs.explain: An irregular pigmented patch on sun-exposed facial skin is lentigo maligna melanoma (best prognosis).

saqs.q: Differentiate the radial and vertical growth phases of melanoma.
List the five clinical types of cutaneous melanoma.
saqs.a: Superficial spreading, lentigo maligna, nodular, acral-lentiginous, mucosal lentiginous.

saqs.q: Expand the ABCDE rule used to screen pigmented lesions.
An older man has an enlarging black nodular lesion of the hard palate. Most likely diagnosis and two typical features?
saqs.a: Oral malignant melanoma. Features: hard palate/maxillary alveolus site, male, older age, flat→nodular, may bleed/ulcerate.

saqs.q: Which cutaneous melanoma has the best, and which the worst, prognosis?
saqs.a: Best: lentigo maligna melanoma. Worst: nodular (and acral-lentiginous) melanoma.

saqs.q: Name three immunohistochemical markers for melanoma and the most sensitive one.
saqs.a: S-100 (~90%), HMB-45 (~95.5%), Melan-A (~100%). Melan-A is essentially 100% positive.
